_comment: Tier-2 for dealii hp_adaptive#3. Tier-2 for dealii hp_adaptive#3 — probe "no_smoothness_estimator" of the shared hp translation unit _shared/hp_family.cc, compiled once and cached so seven fixtures share one build. Eight adaptive cycles on a SMOOTH manufactured solution (u = sin(pi x) sin(pi y), zero Dirichlet), run twice in one process: once with the FESeries::Legendre object driving p-adaptivity, once without it. Without it there is no p-decision to make, every cell stays at FE_Q(1), and the L2 error against the analytic solution falls with the plain h-rate. The entry names a function "p_adaptivity_from_smoothness" that silently falls back to uniform refinement. No such symbol exists in this library — the grep below lists what hp::Refinement actually offers — so the pitfall is the absence of the estimator, not a fallback inside it. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against deal.II 9.8.0-pre (Release at ~/dealii/build; Debug at the dbgbuild tree where the fixture sets requires_debug); every expect_in_output string was copied from that run. MUTATION CONTROL (T2_MUTATE=1, re-runnable; the hook is the export in cmd.sh, the branch itself is mutate() in _shared/hp_family.cc): the mutation hands the run under test the FESeries::Legendre smoothness estimator, so p-adaptivity raises the degree. Three expectations then go missing at once — run_under_test_kept_every_cell_at_the_lowest_degree=true, run_under_test_is_at_least_ten_times_less_accurate=true and run_under_test_used_a_smoothness_estimator=false — and the forbidden VERDICT=p_adaptivity_raised_the_polynomial_degree appears. Proved KILLED 2026-08-07.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: give the run under test the FESeries::Legendre smoothness estimator, so p-adaptivity really does decide
